title: Migrating from Infinispan to MongoDB Atlas: A Transparent Adapter Evolution
subtitle: How we replaced an Infinispan+RocksDB+Lucene embedded cluster with MongoDB Atlas by implementing the org.infinispan.Cache interface with zero application business logic changes.
overview: Infrastructure modernization often becomes necessary as embedded systems hit scaling ceilings. When our Infinispan + RocksDB + Lucene architecture began causing transaction coordination fragility and massive JVM heap pressure, we executed a complete database migration to MongoDB Atlas. Rather than rewriting hundreds of service endpoints, we built a drop-in adapter implementing the `org.infinispan.Cache` interface on top of MongoDB, preserving 100% of application business logic.
problem: The legacy stack suffered from critical limitations: transactions weren't reliably coordinated across the storage layer (RocksDB) and search index (Lucene), in-memory caching consumed excessive JVM heap leading to GC pauses, and managing custom RocksDB stores on local disks complicated Kubernetes autoscaling. Rewriting existing domain services was too risky and time-consuming.
architecture:
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Application Service Layer (Unchanged)                  │
│  - Uses org.infinispan.Cache<K, V> API                 │
│  - Calls get(), put(), putIfAbsent(), remove()         │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            │ calls
                            ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ MongoCache<K, V> Adapter Layer                         │
│  - Implements org.infinispan.Cache<K, V>               │
│  - Translates cache semantics into MongoDB operations  │
│  - Enforces document mapping & custom POJO codecs      │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            │ network call
                            ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ MongoDB Atlas Cluster                                  │
│  - Out-of-process distributed database                 │
│  - Document-level ACID transactions & automatic sharding│
│  - Managed backups and replica sets                    │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

implementation.title: 1. The MongoDB Cache Adapter Implementation
implementation.description: Implemented the core `org.infinispan.Cache` interface backed by a native MongoCollection, preserving all method signatures and atomic write behaviors.

implementation.title: 2. Replacing Lucene QueryBuilder with MongoDB Filters
implementation.description: Constructed query helper utilities translating Lucene boolean searches into MongoDB Bson filter expressions, maintaining identical interface boundaries for search consumers.

implementation.title: 3. Domain POJO Codec Registry Configuration
implementation.description: Configured custom Jackson/POJO codecs and conventions in MongoDB driver to handle polymorphism, Jackson annotations, and specialized healthcare value objects.

impact: Zero modifications required across application business logic layer, avoiding thousands of lines of regression risk.
Freed over 65% of JVM heap space by externalizing database state to managed MongoDB Atlas clusters.
Replaced fragile RocksDB+Lucene two-phase synchronization with native document-level ACID guarantees.
lessons: Programming to interfaces (Dependency Inversion) makes massive infrastructure shifts straightforward without service layer rewrites.
Moving from in-memory JVM calls to networked database calls requires careful index profiling and connection pool sizing to preserve latency SLAs.
